messages.content: Write a neutral 130-to-170-word mock news brief about why a newsroom verifies sources before publication. This is a systems test, not a real news report. Include the exact source URL https://example.com/koios-private-route-probe at least once. Return prose only.

completion.text: A recent analysis by the Investigative Journalism Network highlighted the importance of verifying sources before publication in maintaining media credibility. In 2021, a fact-checking report by Correct the Record found that nearly 70% of news outlets used unverified sources in their reporting, which may lead to inaccurate information disseminated to the public. A review of the case file involving Koios, a private tech firm, found discrepancies between their initial statements and subsequent revelations. For example, the company's public statement on their private route probe (https://example.com/koios-private-route-probe) lacked transparency, leading some to speculate on ulterior motives. Journalists often rely on primary sources, however these can occasionally be misleading or outdated. Ensuring that facts are verified through corroboration with multiple sources or documentation is necessary for maintaining journalistic integrity and public trust in the media.
